raw_case_text:
A 54-year-old female presented to the ED in March 2014 with complaints of a 3-day history of fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anorexia. On evaluation she had dry oral mucosa, and laboratory results demonstrated leukocytosis and elevated serum creatinine, amylase (130 units per liter [u/L]), and lipase (118 u/L). Ultrasound examination revealed evidence of cholelithiasis. The initial diagnostic impression was acute kidney injury with dehydration, IV piperacillin-tazobactam and IV fluids were initiated, and the patient was hospitalized.
On day 3 of hospitalization, the patient developed shortness of breath and had bibasilar crackles. Chest X-ray revealed bilateral confluent alveolar opacities. Echocardiogram demonstrated mild tricuspid and mitral valve regurgitation. Laboratory results demonstrated leukocytosis, a 15% drop in hematocrit, thrombocytopenia, and mildly elevated LFTs. Because of the onset of pulmonary edema, developing acute respiratory distress syndrome and concerns of respiratory tract infection, the patient was transferred to the intensive care unit and placed on oxygen supplementation. Furosemide was given, and antimicrobial therapy was changed to include azithromycin, imipenem, trimethoprine-sulfamethoxazole, linezolid, and oseltamivir. Laboratory results demonstrated worsening leukocytosis and thrombocytopenia and prominently elevated LFTs and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) (9,976 u/L).
The following day she was feeling better, but with mild shortness of breath and continued bibasilar crackles. She continued to improve daily thereafter, was transferred to the regular ward on the seventh hospitalization day, and was discharged home on the 12th day of hospitalization.
All blood and sputum cultures were negative. A serum specimen drawn on the sixth day of symptoms (third day of hospitalization) was negative for Leptospira IgM antibody test performed at a commercial reference laboratory and also negative for mycoplasma IgM antibody and HIV. DNA specific to L. interrogans was detected by PCR in a serum specimen collected on day 2 of illness, which was negative by MAT. Serum collected upon patient discharge had a reciprocal MAT titer of 3,200 against serogroup Australis (serovar Bratislava).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 54-year-old female presenting with a 3-day history of fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anorexia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented in March 2014 with a 3-day history of fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anorexia. She was admitted for dehydration and acute kidney injury. On hospital day 3, she developed acute shortness of breath and bibasilar crackles, with a 15% drop in hematocrit, thrombocytopenia, and bilateral alveolar opacities, prompting ICU transfer for acute respiratory distress syndrome and pulmonary edema. Her condition improved daily thereafter, allowing transfer to the medical ward on day 7 and discharge on day 12.

objective.physical_examination: Initial evaluation: Dry oral mucosa. Hospital day 3: Shortness of breath, bibasilar crackles, requiring supplemental oxygen. Hospital day 4: Mild shortness of breath with continued bibasilar crackles.
objective.routine_investigations:
Initial laboratory results: Leukocytosis, elevated serum creatinine, elevated amylase (130 u/L), and elevated lipase (118 u/L). Abdominal ultrasound: Cholelithiasis.
Hospital day 3: Leukocytosis, 15% drop in hematocrit, thrombocytopenia, and mildly elevated LFTs. Chest X-ray: Bilateral confluent alveolar opacities.
Follow-up labs: Worsening leukocytosis, worsening thrombocytopenia, prominently elevated LFTs, and markedly elevated LDH (9,976 u/L).
Negative routine infectious workup: Sputum and blood cultures were negative; serum Mycoplasma IgM and HIV screening were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Echocardiogram: Mild tricuspid and mitral valve regurgitation.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Confirmed Leptospira interrogans infection (leptospirosis) complicated by acute kidney injury, pancreatitis, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and pulmonary edema. Confirmed by positive PCR detection of L. interrogans DNA in serum collected on illness day 2 (initial MAT negative), followed by convalescent MAT reciprocal titer of 3,200 against serogroup Australis (serovar Bratislava) at discharge. Commercial serum Leptospira IgM on symptom day 6 was negative. Blood cultures, sputum cultures, Mycoplasma IgM, and HIV were negative.
Plan & Outcome: Initial therapy with IV fluids and IV piperacillin-tazobactam. Following ARDS/pulmonary edema onset in the ICU, managed with oxygen supplementation, IV furosemide, and expanded antimicrobial coverage with azithromycin, imipenem, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, linezolid, and oseltamivir. The patient achieved full clinical resolution and was discharged home on hospital day 12.
